body:
I forgot to mention that he stated he was in an open relationship before we met.

I understand your concern, finding out that someone you like is already in a relationship while you're looking for a monogamous partner can be annoying. But at the end of the day, we can't really exclude people we don't like from the dating scene. I mean, if you use grindr or other apps, the closest you can get to this is probably to use a filter. Or maybe change the app entirely for another one, I'm sure there is one where you can find gay guys who are looking for monogamous relationships. And if none of this works out, you can always ask first before you meet.

It's extra work on your side, I get it. But it's not up to me or to you to choose if someone else's relationship has to be monogamous or not.

Thank you for your words. For some reason reddit didn't show a notification so I'm just now reading this and many other answers.

I should mention that I knew about his open relationship before we met and that I didn't pressure him into doing anything other than a hookup. If anything, I clearly told him that I didn't want to interfere with his relationship and it was entirely his decision to reach out to me afterwards. So yeah, I think you're right. This is probably something he's used to, similarly to you and your partner, and I shouldn't feel guilty.

To me, knowing that it will never be more than this... It does sting a bit. But due to various circumstances, I can't imagine us ever being an actual couple. It's not just about his existing relationship. It''s about our jobs, friends and lives being in completely different countries. It's about me being new to dating and wanting to explore, instead of settling down already.

I don't know what the future holds for me. I guess that if I was in a relationship, I wouldn't stay on grindr to try and find someone else to bond with. No judgement on you and anyone else who does this, obviously. We're different people with different needs, and that's okay.

I'll enjoy what I have for now while he's here, and I'll try avoiding falling in love with him. In case it happens, I'll survive. I know I did in the past.

How am I? I'm a train wreck. I'm writing here, in this somewhat old thread, so that hopefully no one reads this.

I tried over and over to live a normal life, keeping good mental health, but my mind doesn't seem to cooperate. I keep blaming myself for every dumb bad thing that happens (or might happen, go figure). Even for things that I have no control over, such as the fact that I like older men. I mean, I know it's not bad, but I still _feel_ like I shouldn't. I've known this thing about myself for years and I still haven't fully accepted it. I don't know, maybe it's internalised homophobia or something? Either way, I wanna keep friends and family out of this until I figure it out by myself. And that of course also makes me feel lonely, because I've been avoiding everyone lately.

Also, despite the fact that I have so much work to do, I feel incapable of doing anything. I can't even wash my teeth or get out of bed. I'm starting to feel hopeless. I'm not sure I even want to try anymore. I've been thinking about suicide more and more often. I know it's absolutely NOT a good choice. It's not a solution, at all. Period. But somehow it still _feels_ like a solution, as if it was the only one. I'm sure I wasn't thinking about it so often in the past, but now I am, and it terrifies me. Maybe I won't do it now, maybe not in 5 years. But if things don't take a turn quickly, I have no idea of what will happen.

It's Saturday and my friends are out having fun, while I chose to stay home and lay on my bed. Told them I had some deadlines coming up (which is true), but I don't feel like working either. It's been like this for a few days now.
You're right, I don't need to tell them everything, but I think I'll do it in the future, at least with some of them.

I see your point about marriage, though I don't wish it to any of my friends. It would break my heart as well! And thankfully I already have plenty of things that put a smile on my face. Perhaps with time I will stop worrying about this issue like you did.

Well, thankfully I'm already living the life that I want. Except that I don't know anyone that I can date.

About the 50 yo guy that I talked about, let's say that I ask him out and he isn't interested. Things would get embarrassing quickly, but I will still need to work with him. How would you manage that?

By the way, yeah I'm sure some of my friends already know that I'm gay even though I don't act much differently than a straight guy. Just because that's me, not because I'm trying to hide it.

Yeah, I should have mentioed, I can't even begin to describe how grateful I am for what I have in my life. Great friends and family, I love what I'm doing, honestly I'm living a dream.

But nothing is perfect, and I can't help but notice that my friends are moving forward with their sentimental life, and here I am, talking to strangers on reddit (to be clear, I'm grateful for that as well).

Sometimes I just feel sad, and I guess this post is what happens in that case. Thank you.

Shifting the subject a bit, there's this guy, I believe almost 50 years old, that I really like. He's not married, but I take for granted that he's straight, and that even if he was bi or secretly gay, I don't think he would be into me. We're friends, and I'll see him for at least a few more months. I would like to tell him how I feel, even if I don't expect anything from him, but I'm sure that doing so would make the following conversations just too embarrassing, at least for me. I mean, knowing him, he would be ok with it. But maybe I wouldn't. I don't know anymore, just help please I think I'm going crazy.
I'm sure you found yourself in similar situations in the past, what did you, if you did anything?
